Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Assessment consistent with classical migraine headache:
  - Unilateral left-sided throbbing headache with visual aura (zig-zag lines), photophobia, nausea, and vomiting  
  - No neurological deficits (no weakness, numbness, speech or balance problems)  
  - Family history of migraines supportive  
- DDx includes:
  - Migraine (High likelihood): supported by classic symptoms and family history  
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (Medium likelihood): oral contraceptive use plus headache worsening on neck movement raise suspicion; however, no neurological deficits or worsening signs reduce likelihood; to be monitored  
  - Brain tumor (Low to Medium likelihood): patient concern noted; visual disturbances and headache worsening with movement present but no progression or focal deficits argue against aggressive tumor presently  
  - Meningitis (Low likelihood): headache, photophobia, vomiting present but no fever or neck stiffness  
  - Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (Low likelihood): visual symptoms and headache pattern noted but no papilledema or other IIH signs documented  
- Other possible contributors: stress-induced headache related to occupational stress; medication side effects less likely but noted (OCP)  
- Conflict noted: DDx raises CVST and brain tumor risks; transcript favors migraine and reassurance without investigations reported  

Management Plan
- Initiate symptomatic treatment with strong painkillers: paracetamol, co-codamol, and anti-inflammatory agents such as ibuprofen or naproxen as tolerated  
- Maintain headache diary to identify triggers and monitor headache pattern  
- Educate patient about warning signs requiring urgent review: worsening or persistent headache beyond 2–3 days, new neurological symptoms (weakness, vision changes), worsening neck pain  
- Arrange follow-up appointment in one week to reassess and consider prophylactic migraine treatment if headaches persist or worsen  
- No investigations or imaging currently ordered; consider if clinical status changes  
- Address stress management, discuss possibility of lifestyle modifications (exercise encouraged, counseling if needed)  
- Continue oral contraceptive pill as per patient preference, but monitor symptoms due to potential risk with OCP
